title: Chocolate Cookies
description: Deliciously rich and chewy chocolate cookies, loaded with chocolate chips.
author: Chris Garza
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, cream together softened butter, white sugar, and brown sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the egg and vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined.
Fold in chocolate chips if using.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the prepared baking sheet (about 1.5-inch balls).
Bake for 8–10 minutes, until the edges are set. The cookies will continue to cook on the sheet.
Let the cookies cool for a few minutes on the baking sheet, then transfer to a wire rack.

title: Cilantro Crema
author: Jackie's Mimaw
instructions: Sear peppers on a cast iron skillet or in a toaster oven. Cut and remove seeds.
Add all ingredients to a blender or food processor and blend until creamy and smooth.
tips: If you want a spicy version, add a serrano.

title: Migas and Bacon
description: A simple Tex-Mex breakfast dish featuring fried tortilla strips scrambled with eggs, served alongside crispy bacon.
author: Jackie's Mimaw
instructions: Cut bacon slices in half, cut tortillas into squares, and whisk eggs with pepper in a separate bowl.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add bacon and cook until dark or lightly blackened, keeping the skillet covered.
Remove bacon to a paper towel-lined plate.
Add tortilla squares to the skillet and stir, increasing heat slightly.
Once sizzling, reduce heat, remove tortillas to a plate, and lightly salt.
Add butter to the pan and let it melt.
Add the egg mixture and cook on medium-low heat, covered.
When the eggs are mostly cooked, stir in the tortilla squares and serve with bacon.

title: Mexican Buñuelos
description: Crispy golden fried dough discs tossed in aromatic cinnamon and sugar—a beloved festive Mexican treat.
author: Jackie's Family
instructions: In a bowl, mix flour, baking powder, salt, and 1 tbsp sugar. Add warm water and oil, kneading until smooth and soft (about 5 minutes).
Divide into 12 balls, cover with a towel, and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each ball into a very thin circular disc on a lightly floured surface.
Heat frying oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat (375°F / 190°C).
Fry discs one at a time for about 60 seconds per side until crispy and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels for a few seconds, then immediately dredge both sides in the cinnamon-sugar mixture.
tips: The thinner you roll the dough discs, the crispier and airier the buñuelos will be.

title: Smoked Sausage & Okra Skillet
description: Sizzling smoked sausage slices sautéed with fresh sliced okra, onions, and bold Creole seasoning.
author: Jackie's Family
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced smoked sausage and cook until nicely browned on both sides (about 5-6 minutes). Remove sausage from skillet.
Add remaining oil, diced onion, and okra to the hot skillet.
Cook okra and onions for 8 to 10 minutes until okra edges are tender-crisp and browned.
Stir in minced garlic, Creole seasoning, and diced tomatoes. Cook for 3 minutes.
Return browned sausage back to the skillet and toss everything together to heat through.
Serve hot over steamed white rice or with cornbread.
tips: Cooking okra over high heat without overcrowding reduces slime and yields a crispy, caramelized texture.

title: Traditional Pork Tamales
description: Savory shredded pork slow-cooked in a red chile sauce, enclosed in tender corn masa and steamed in corn husks.
author: Jackie's Family

ingredients.item: cooked shredded pork in red chile

instructions: Soak corn husks in hot water for at least 30 minutes until pliable. Pat dry.
Beat lard in a stand mixer on medium-high until light, fluffy, and white (about 5 minutes).
Gradually add masa harina, baking powder, and salt. Slowly pour in warm broth while beating until a smooth, spreadable paste forms.
Spread about 3 tablespoons of masa onto the smooth side of each husk, leaving the top third and side edges clear.
Spoon 2 tablespoons of shredded red chile pork down the center of the masa.
Fold one side over the meat, fold the other side over, then fold the narrow bottom tip upwards.
Stand tamales upright (open end up) in a steamer pot filled with water below the steamer rack.
Cover and steam over medium-low heat for 60 to 90 minutes, until the husk peels cleanly away from the masa.
Let rest for 15 minutes before unwrapping and serving.
tips: Test the masa: drop a small ½ tsp ball into a cup of cold water. If it floats to the top, your masa is light enough and ready to spread!
